patches.expect: Drive the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to its end at Artist Point. Start on Chain Lakes Trail 682 for about a mile to the Ptarmigan Ridge junction, then follow Ptarmigan Ridge Trail 682.1 along the crest, passing beneath Coleman Pinnacle, to Camp Kiser at roughly 5 miles. Past Camp Kiser the maintained tread ends and a primitive climbers' boot path takes over. Leave the crest on snow to climber's right, traverse below the ridgeline to a rocky saddle, cross to its far side and work beneath the cliff bands down onto the Rainbow Glacier. Cross the Rainbow and climb onto the Park Glacier; most parties camp near The Portals. From camp, ascend the Park Glacier through the crevasses toward the Park Glacier Headwall, with the Cockscomb rising above it, and follow the ridge to the summit plateau. Note that the Coleman and Roosevelt Glaciers are on Baker's west and northwest flanks and are not crossed on this approach.

From camp, rope up and cross the Coleman and then the Roosevelt Glacier heading northeast — roughly 2-3 hours of crevassed travel — and take low-to-moderate snow ramps to the foot of the ridge at about 7,500-7,800 ft. Thin snow bridges over a crevasse maze are the main hazard on this crossing.

patches.expect:
The same walk in as the Park Glacier Headwall: Chain Lakes Trail 682 from Artist Point for about a mile to the Ptarmigan Ridge junction, then Trail 682.1 along the crest past Coleman Pinnacle to Camp Kiser at roughly five miles. Past Camp Kiser the maintained trail ends and a primitive bootpath takes over through the Portals.

From there leave the crest on snow, traverse below the ridgeline to a rocky saddle, cross to its far side, work beneath the cliff bands down onto the Rainbow Glacier, cross it and climb onto the Park Glacier. Camps are usually near the Portals.

Snow lingers here into late season, which makes the walk long early and the navigation harder later.
patches.value:
Glacier Creek Road (FR 39) to the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead, then Trail 677 through old growth to the fork at about two miles. Take the right-hand climbers' path up the crest of the Hogsback moraine to the camps near 6,000 ft beside the Coleman Glacier, the same camp used for the Coleman-Deming and the North Ridge.

From camp the route ropes up and heads northeast, crossing the Coleman and then the Roosevelt Glacier. Expect two to three hours of glacier travel through a crevasse field before low-to-moderate snow ramps lead to the foot of the ridge.

patches.expect:
The Cockscomb is the formation above the Park Glacier Headwall — the ridge is gained by going up the Park Glacier through the crevasses toward the headwall with the Cockscomb standing above it, then following the ridge to the summit plateau.

Use the Cockscomb itself as the aiming mark rather than any point on the glacier: it is the only thing on this side of the mountain that reads as a serrated rock crest above a headwall. If you are on a glacier with no rock crest above the wall in front of you, you are on the Rainbow rather than the Park and have not finished the crossing.

One durable negative check: the Coleman and Roosevelt Glaciers lie on Baker's west and north-west flanks and are not crossed on this approach at any point.
patches.value:
The ridge is reached by traversing northeast from the Hogsback camps across the Coleman and then the Roosevelt Glacier. Aim for the foot of the ridge at about 7,500-7,800 ft, where low-angle snow ramps lead up onto the crest.

The Cockscomb Tower, about 300 ft high, stands well above the base and is passed on its east side by steep snow; if you are already beside it, you are far above the start. If you have crossed only the Coleman and are still west of the Roosevelt, you have not reached this ridge yet.
